transcript.text: f/f freezer keeps icing up bottom drawer wont shut proper, defrosted it 2wks ago already full of ice again. indesit

Ice returning within two weeks is not normal. The two most likely causes are a freezer door that is not sealing properly, letting damp room air in, or an automatic-defrost fault. 1. Switch it off and check the freezer door first: remove anything fouling the drawer or door, then inspect the rubber seal all the way round for a split, gap, fold or section pulled away. Also look whether the door has dropped or sits out of line. A poor seal can create enough ice to stop the bottom drawer closing. 2. Look at where the ice forms. If it is mainly a thick solid sheet on the rear inside panel of the freezer, that points more towards the defrost system — typically the defrost heater, sensor/thermal thermostat, or control/timer. A manual defrost temporarily clears it, but it will return until the failed defrost component is identified and repaired. If the seal looks damaged or the door is sagging, that is the first thing to rectify. If the seal looks sound and the rear panel is repeatedly becoming a solid ice block, an engineer is the sensible next step; the exact defrost part cannot be confirmed without testing and depends on the full model number.

ok checked. bottom corner of freezer door seal is split about 5cm and the hinge side bottom bit is flattened. ice mostly round front edge and bottom drawer, thick frost. can i replace the seal myself?

[Heading: Likely cause: door seal]
Yes — replacing a freezer door seal is usually a reasonable DIY job, provided the replacement is matched to the full model number. Your split corner and flattened hinge-side section are very likely letting warm, damp kitchen air into the freezer, which explains the heavy frost around the front and bottom drawer. First, get the full Indesit model number from the rating label, usually inside the fridge compartment on a side wall near the salad drawer. It can wait if the label is awkward to reach. When you have the correct seal, switch the appliance off and unplug it. Seals are commonly either pushed into a retaining channel or secured behind the inner door liner; do not force the door liner or use a knife to prise around it. Warm the new seal gently in a warm room or with warm water so it sits flat, fit it evenly all the way round, then close the door and check there are no gaps. A sheet of paper should feel lightly gripped at several points around the seal. Because there is already thick ice, do a full defrost and dry the freezer before fitting the seal; otherwise the drawer may still foul even with the new gasket. If the door remains dropped, twisted, or will not line up after the seal is replaced, the hinge/alignment will need attention instead.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
ok will read the rating plate. its an Indesit IB55532W. what do i search for to buy the seal?

[Heading: Likely cause: door seal]
Search for: “Indesit IB55532W freezer door seal” or “Indesit IB55532W freezer door gasket”. I cannot confirm a catalogue match for that exact model reference, so do not order solely from a photo or from the appliance colour. Use the full rating-plate details with Indesit’s official spares service or a reputable spares supplier, and check the listing explicitly states compatibility with the complete model/product code from the label. The gasket needs to match both the door size and the way it attaches. The split corner and flattened hinge-side section make the seal the leading cause of the rapid frost build-up. Before buying it, check whether the door itself closes fully and lines up: if it is dropped or catches on the hinge side, a new seal alone may not cure the gap. If it shuts squarely but the rubber is split, replacing the freezer door gasket is the sensible repair.
